doc.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024

title: Pop influences: Elton John, Carole King, Joni Mitchell songs
summary: Rowe's pop influences include Carole King, James Taylor and Elton John, and her sparse trio arrangement of 'Both Sides Now'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Did the pop music you listened to as a kid have any influence on your writing?

It definitely did, and I’m still perfectly happy to just write a tune and, you know, in a style that may be more folk or folk-jazz influenced or whatever it might be. But yeah, Carole King, Carly Simon, James Taylor, Elton John — you know the first thing I figured out how to play on the piano, a kind of a pop tune, was “Your Song” by Elton John. And I loved the way he played, I loved his melodicism, and there’s some — I don’t want to say any of that music is simple. I mean it might not be as — you know there might not be as many sharp elevens and flat nines and this and that, but just the beauty of it, the way it was put together. I mean “Both Sides Now” I just did a trio arrangement on that and every — and again the whole focus on the trio arrangement is to leave lots of space and quiet and just to let the tune kind of speak for itself with a few re-harmonizations here
and there. But yeah, no I love that music and it’s still is big part I think of who I am as a musician.
